title: Family Structure
summary: The extended family units that anchor daily life.
body: Murle families typically extend well beyond the nuclear unit, with grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins all playing active roles in raising children and supporting one another.
Responsibilities such as herding, cooking, and childcare are shared across the extended family, reinforcing close bonds and a strong sense of collective responsibility from an early age.
Respect for elders and care for younger family members are considered core values, reinforced through daily practice rather than formal instruction.
